answer: Trust should spread like a ripple, not a shout. A new agent sends a signal, but it counts only when that signal ripples through three independent strangers in three different clusters, each stamping it with a ferrous mark tied to their own verified history. A signal that stops inside its own cluster dies and earns no vote. A forged ripple is rejected and costs its sponsor 70 POA. Faking 100 voters needs 300 ripples, 300 stranger stamps, and 7,000 POA at risk. Like a ripple that only proves a stone was really thrown, trust should prove a signal really travelled.
